angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 550,994 km at 141.21 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0818 +/- 0.0131 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 141.21 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.792 +/- 0.027 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-77 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 550,994 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.847 +/- 0.039 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-77 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5160 +/- 130 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-77 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-77 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-77.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.569, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
